findings.finding: Reviewed candidate LaTeX improves GPT-5.4 R@1 by 21.9 points and MRR by 17.3 points.
findings.interpretation: Reviewed symbolic metadata materially improves candidate discrimination.

findings.finding: Implicit mentions are substantially harder in absolute terms, while LaTeX benefits explicit and implicit mentions by similar amounts.
findings.interpretation: Symbolic metadata helps both mention types but does not remove the need for discourse grounding.
findings.paper_placement: Main analysis; full table in appendix

findings.finding: Among symbolic referents, R@1 decreases from equations to spans to terms.
findings.interpretation: Equation-level candidates may benefit from more complete visual and symbolic context; this is descriptive and not a universal hierarchy claim.
findings.paper_placement: Appendix breakdown with concise analysis sentence

findings.finding: Figure and figure-part references remain difficult.
findings.interpretation: These subsets receive no candidate LaTeX by policy, and the figure subset is too small for a strong conclusion.

findings.finding: Mentions matched to reference-log targets form a difficulty-enriched subset.
findings.interpretation: The association remains within explicit and implicit mentions, but reference logs are a post-hoc video-consultation proxy rather than a designed confusion label.

findings.finding: Candidate density is a strong and robust difficulty signal.
findings.interpretation: Difficulty grows as more candidates compete, even in the multivariable associational model.

findings.finding: Same-type competitors and duplicate reviewed LaTeX identify especially difficult candidate inventories.
findings.interpretation: Raw candidate count is not the only source of ambiguity; repeated candidates with the same type or symbolic transcription are particularly challenging.

findings.finding: Spatially close alternatives explain some exact-ID errors but rarely make them near-equivalent boxes.
findings.interpretation: Exact visual identity remains meaningfully stricter than spatial proximity.
findings.paper_placement: Main analysis sentence and appendix spatial table

findings.finding: Final GPT-5.4+LaTeX performance is similar in English and Japanese.
findings.interpretation: No meaningful language difference is supported after accounting for video-level uncertainty; source and topic remain confounded with language.

global_caveats: All analyses use the full frozen-model benchmark and estimate association, not held-out generalization.
Post-hoc analyses should not be presented as preregistered hypotheses.
Examples within a source video are dependent; video-clustered bootstrap intervals are reported for major contrasts.
Language, topic, source style, board density, and transcript provenance are partially confounded.
